text:
Softmax over real history forces total weight one: equally irrelevant logits yield uniform pooling, and lowering every logit equally changes nothing. Zero output remains possible through value cancellation, but weights cannot reject all history. Original [DIN](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.06978) deliberately omits softmax, preserving interest intensity; unnormalized activations can all approach zero, although this is learned, not guaranteed, and aggregation can depend on history length. A zero-valued null slot instead gives αᵢ=exp(sᵢ)/(exp(s₀)+Σⱼexp(sⱼ)): real-history mass approaches zero when the null dominates. Null value must remain zero after projection; finite softmax logits generally provide approximate abstention. Related precedent: [attention heads learning no-op updates](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/edbcb7583fd8921dad78adecfe06a99b-Abstract-Conference.html).

Asymmetric candidate–history bilinear scoring is established sequential modeling: [FPMC](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=50d85cb114f7c5e779a6772f2931e77dddd54a5e&repid=rep1&type=pdf) combines user–candidate preference with separately factorized previous-item→candidate transitions. [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.09152) combines FISM history aggregation with personalized higher-order Markov weights, sharing history/target factors across long- and short-term terms. Its separate P/Q embeddings permit directional interactions. Candidate-dependent attention adds adaptive history weighting beyond these bilinear precedents.

Algebraic control: with column embeddings, attention logits cᵀQᵀKh are symmetric iff QᵀK is symmetric; Q=K suffices. For scalar residual cᵀRᵀΣᵢαᵢVhᵢ, also require RᵀV symmetric; tying Q=K alone leaves value-side directionality. A sufficient control ties Q=K and R=V, uses shared item embeddings and symmetric pairwise gates, and removes role-specific biases. Even then, history-wise softmax denominators, recency weights, and contextual history encoders can break exchange symmetry. Claim symmetric pairwise compatibility unless the complete residual is invariant under candidate/history exchange.
